license.name: Non-commercial / no SLA / experimental
license.attribution: Airplanes.live globe web snapshot. Non-commercial only; no SLA; no completeness claims.
license.caveat: This is the experimental globe web JSON consumed by globe.airplanes.live. It is a derived snapshot of the same upstream ADS-B/MLAT receiver network, with no documented SLA, no completeness claims, and no formal agreement for non-commercial embedding. Use the canonical Airplanes.live REST API v2 (source_id 'airplanes_live_v2') for production-grade live tracking.

attribution_required: Appreciated; no formal requirement. UI must still display the non-commercial / no-SLA caveat (see ADR-002).
what_it_provides: Global gzip-compressed JSON snapshot of all currently visible aircraft on the globe.airplanes.live site. Carries the same per-aircraft fields as the REST v2 endpoints but in a single global payload. Used for low-latency global visibility when the global view is required (not just camera-region /point).
fields_collected: Same shape as the per-record REST v2 payload (hex / flight / r / t / lat / lon / alt_baro / alt_geom / gs / track / mag_heading / true_heading / baro_rate / geom_rate / squawk / emergency / seen / seen_pos / type / dbFlags)

refresh_policy.schedule_note: Worker supports --loop with a fixed-rate 5-second cycle. The cycle is split into Phase A (fetch), Phase B (build compact payload), Phase C (publish live snapshot — high priority), and Phase D (write raw/latest/observations — lower priority, every N cycles). 403/429/500/502/503/504 responses trigger a 30s backoff (GLOBAL_WEB_JSON_BACKOFF_SECONDS). Polling more aggressively than every 5s may be blocked or rate-limited by the upstream; this is the documented minimum.

freshness_policy.notes: Same staleness thresholds as airplanes_live_v2 (STALE_ACTIVE_THRESHOLD=30, STALE_FADE_THRESHOLD=90, STALE_PURGE_THRESHOLD=300).

raw_storage.bucket: n/a (no raw blob persisted; per-record JSONB in aviation_aircraft_raw_batches.raw_sample)
raw_storage.path_pattern: not applicable — see aviation_aircraft_raw_batches table instead
raw_storage.notes: fetch_params JSONB stores {"sourceMode": "global-web-json"} and the upstream 'messages' counter so the snapshot provenance is preserved.

collector.name: aviation_live_aircraft_worker (global-web-json mode)
collector.db_writes_use_source_id: airplanes_live_v2 (DEFAULT_SOURCE_ID) — the worker intentionally aligns DB rows with the REST source id so the API/WebSocket contract is single-sourced; sourceMode is preserved in fetch_params / snapshot metadata.

normalizer.name: normalize_aircraft (inline in worker)
normalizer.notes: Live aircraft normalization is performed inline in the worker. The compact payload for the live snapshot table is also built inline (avoids a round trip through services/normalizer/).

target_tables: aviation_aircraft_sources (no separate row; DB writes use source_id='airplanes_live_v2')

api_endpoints.notes: The REST and WebSocket surfaces are single-sourced on source_id='airplanes_live_v2' even when the worker is running in global-web-json mode. The sourceMode distinction is preserved in fetch_params and snapshot metadata for provenance.

frontend_usage.transport: WebSocket (snapshot + delta) for live, REST for latest-list / detail
frontend_usage.notes: The frontend does not branch on sourceMode; the visible aircraft set is whatever the worker last persisted to aviation_aircraft_latest and pushed into the broadcaster.

known_limitations: Experimental / dev source. No SLA, no completeness claim. The snapshot may be rate-limited or blocked; the worker must respect 30s backoff on 403/429/5xx.
Polling faster than every 5 seconds is unsafe — upstream may block. GLOBAL_WEB_JSON_MIN_INTERVAL_SECONDS=5 is enforced.

DB rows are intentionally written with source_id='airplanes_live_v2' (not this catalog source_id) to keep the API/WebSocket contract single-sourced. SourceMode is preserved in fetch_params and snapshot metadata only.
Not for production-grade live tracking; use airplanes_live_v2 (REST mode) for that. This mode exists for low-latency global snapshots where the global view is required.
ui_caveat: When this source is active, the same non-commercial / no-SLA caveat as airplanes_live_v2 applies. The frontend does not need a separate 'sourceMode' badge in the current build.
notes: Treated as a distinct upstream source/mode at the source-catalog level so future agents can see it separately from the REST v2 source.
Internally the worker uses GLOBAL_WEB_JSON_SOURCE_ID = 'airplanes_live_global_web_json' for parameter naming, but DB writes go to source_id='airplanes_live_v2' (DEFAULT_SOURCE_ID).

If a future build decides to expose this source as a distinct source_id in the API/WebSocket contract, an additional DB row in aviation_aircraft_sources and a corresponding migration will be needed; today the sourceMode is provenance only.
